question: In the MRI safety zone classification, Zone IV (the magnet room itself) is the most restricted area because the static magnetic field is always present and any ferromagnetic object — including a steel oxygen cylinder — becomes a high-velocity projectile the moment it enters the room, regardless of whether a scan is in progress.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The MRI magnet is always on. Zone IV danger is not limited to scan time. A ferromagnetic object — cylinder, trolley, IV pole — accelerates toward the bore as soon as it crosses into Zone IV, which is why MR-Conditional equipment and strict zone access control are non-negotiable.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The static field in Zone IV is always on — there is no 'off switch' between scans. A steel oxygen cylinder brought into Zone IV by a nurse in a hurry (as in the hook story) becomes a projectile instantly. This is why all equipment entering Zone IV must be labelled MR-Conditional or MR-Safe.
